description: Learn how to download Canva desktop app on Mac from canva.com or the App Store, then open it past Apple's first-open warning.

intro: Download the Canva desktop app for Mac from canva.com/download/mac, or install the Mac listing from the Mac App Store, then open Canva from your Applications folder. The app requires macOS 13.0 or later and supports both Apple silicon and Intel Macs, and if macOS blocks the first launch, you allow it in System Settings under Privacy & Security.
tldr: Download from canva.com/download/mac, or install the Mac listing from the App Store.
Canva for Mac needs macOS 13.0 or later and supports Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
If Apple blocks the first open, go to System Settings > Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.
Check for updates from the Canva menu for canva.com installs, or from the App Store's Updates tab.

blocks.text: Canva's desktop app for Mac comes from two places. You can download the Mac file from canva.com, or you can install the app from the Mac App Store. This guide covers both routes, the Apple warning you may see on the first open, how to update later, and the problems people hit most often. I checked the pages on 9 November 2026, so the version numbers below are from that date.
Check that your Mac can run Canva

Start with the macOS version, because it decides everything else. Click the Apple menu in the top left corner and choose About This Mac. Read the macOS line in the window that opens. The Mac App Store listing says Canva requires macOS 13.0 or later, so treat 13.0 as the minimum.

Older guides and search snippets list older macOS versions, such as 11, 12 or 10.15. Those numbers come from third-party sites and older listings. The current App Store listing is the better source, because it shows a version number and a release date. When two sources disagree, trust the newer one that names its version.

You don't need to pick a chip type. Canva's download page says the app is available for Macs with Intel chips and Apple chips. The download link path says universal, which suggests one file covers both. If you want to confirm your chip, About This Mac shows that too. The check takes a few seconds.

items: macOS 13.0 or later, shown under Apple menu > About This Mac.

About 168 MB of download space, based on the Mac App Store listing.
Access to canva.com and the Mac App Store. Some work networks block one or both.
Permission to change Privacy & Security settings. A managed Mac may not give you that.

blocks.text: Check the list before you start a download. A work Mac may block installs from outside the App Store, and that changes the route you should take. If you're on a company device, read the section on managed Macs first, so you don't waste a download.
How to download Canva desktop app on Mac

Open Safari, or another browser you already use, and go to canva.com/download/mac. Type the address yourself if a link in an email or chat looks odd. Click Download Canva for Mac. That button links to canva.com/download/mac/universal/canva-desktop.

The download page doesn't show a version number, a file type, or install steps. So the steps below follow the usual Mac pattern. If the file is a disk image that ends in .dmg, open it and drag Canva onto the Applications folder. If the file is already an app, move it into Applications. Either way, Applications is where Canva should end up.
Watch the download in your browser until it finishes. Keep the Mac awake during the download. Don't open a half-finished file, because the copy can be incomplete and fail in confusing ways later.

Canva's help center returned an error when I checked it, so I couldn't confirm the official install steps there. If the file you downloaded looks different from this guide, check canva.com/help for the desktop app article before you go on.

blocks.text: Install Canva from the Mac App Store

The App Store route works well if you want updates in one place. Open the App Store app and search for Canva. Choose the Mac listing from developer Canva, with seller Canva Pty Ltd. The listing I checked shows version 1.127.0, released November 1, and a download size of 167.9 MB.

Click the button that offers the app, such as Get or Install, depending on what you see. Wait for the download to finish. Then open Canva from Applications, not from the download window, so you always launch the installed copy.

Check the listing before you click. The Canva iPhone page uses the same app ID, 897446215, but it shows a different version, 4.234.0. If you see that version number on a Mac, you're on the wrong page.
Which route should you pick?

Pick the App Store if you want Apple to handle updates in one place. Pick canva.com if you already work from the website and prefer a direct file. The sources I checked don't confirm that both files carry the same version. Choose one route and stick with it, since two copies can make updates confusing.
Open Canva past the Apple warning

macOS checks apps the first time you open them. If Apple can't check Canva, you may see an alert that reads Apple cannot check Canva for malicious software. The alert has two buttons, Move to Trash and Done. Apple says known malware is moved to the Trash.

blocks.title: Stop if the file came from elsewhere
blocks.text: If you see that alert and you did not download Canva from canva.com or the App Store, move the file to the Trash. Then download again from one of those two pages.

If you downloaded from canva.com or the App Store, the alert is a first-open check, not a verdict on the app. Re-download the file once and try again. Don't keep retrying a file you can't trace, because repeated attempts won't change what macOS checks.

When macOS blocks the first open, use Privacy & Security. Click the Apple menu, then click System Settings. In the sidebar, click Privacy & Security. Scroll down to the message about Canva and click Open Anyway. Then click Open when the warning appears again.
Apple says the app is then saved as an exception, so you should only need to do this once. The step is the same on Apple silicon and Intel Macs, because the check applies to the app, not the chip.

If you can't find Open Anyway, check the setting called Allow apps downloaded from. It has two options, App Store and App Store and identified developers. An administrator may have turned that setting off. In that case the Mac is probably managed, and IT has to approve Canva for you.
Mistakes people make on the first install

items: Downloading from a search result instead of canva.com or the App Store. Type the address or open the App Store yourself.
Installing both copies. A canva.com copy and an App Store copy can both sit in Applications, which makes updates confusing. Keep one.
Launching Canva from the Downloads folder. Open the copy in Applications, so updates and the first-open approval apply to the app you use.
Trashing a file from the right source. If the file came from canva.com or the App Store, the alert is a check, not a final verdict.
Retrying the same blocked file again and again without trying the Privacy & Security step once.
Trusting an older macOS guide. Check the App Store listing for the current minimum version.

blocks.text: Most of these mistakes cost minutes, not data. The fix is usually to slow down at the Applications step and stick to one source. If you're unsure which copy you have, open Applications in Finder and check the app before you update it.
Update the Canva desktop app on Mac
Updates follow how you installed the app. App Store installs update from the App Store. Open the App Store, click Updates in the sidebar, and click Update next to Canva.
Installs from canva.com use the Canva menu. Click Canva in the menu bar and choose Check for Updates. That item appears only when an update exists, so a missing item means nothing is waiting.

That menu path comes from a third-party guide last updated in October 2024. It names no Canva version number. To compare, open the App Store listing and check the version it shows, which was 1.127.0 when I checked.

If you aren't sure which route you used, look in the App Store's Updates tab first. If Canva appears there, the App Store copy is the one you use. If it doesn't, the copy in Applications most likely came from canva.com.
Common install problems and fixes

Most install problems come from three things: the wrong listing, an older macOS, or a managed Mac. Start with the listing, since it's the quickest check. A version number that doesn't match the Mac listing usually points to the wrong page.

Next, check macOS. The Mac listing requires macOS 13.0 or later. If your Mac runs an older release, update macOS first, if the Mac can take the update. If it can't, the desktop app won't run on that Mac.
Third, a managed Mac can block the Open Anyway step. Ask the person who manages the Mac to approve Canva. Don't try to work around the setting on a company device.
Does the Canva desktop app need the internet?

The sources I checked agree that most features need an internet connection. They disagree on speed and offline use, so my notes don't settle it. If you work somewhere with poor signal, test the app first. Open a design, turn off Wi-Fi, and see what still works.
A worked example: installing on a work laptop

Say you open the Canva download page on a work MacBook. You click Download Canva for Mac, open the file, and drag Canva into Applications. Then the Apple warning appears. Your first stop is Privacy & Security. If Open Anyway isn't there, the setting Allow apps downloaded from is probably managed by IT.

Send IT the canva.com download link and the name of the Mac listing from developer Canva. Ask them to approve the app. Once they do, the same steps work. You don't need a second copy, and you shouldn't install one from a different site to get around the block.
Canva Mac keyboard shortcuts to learn first

A few shortcuts save the most time once the app is installed. Undo is ⌘Z and Redo is ⌘Y. Search Canva is ⌘F, which helps when the template library gets long. Fit To Screen is ⌘0, which resets the view after you zoom.
Try them on a real design. Zoom in with ⌘+ to nudge a small label. Press ⌘0 to see the whole page again. If the nudge went too far, press ⌘Z to undo it.

For repeat layouts, select elements and press ⌘G to group them. Press ⌘D to duplicate a selected element. Ungroup with ⌘⇧G when you need to edit one part of the set. These shortcuts come from a third-party cheat sheet, not Canva's own list, so test each one.
What to do next after the install

Open a blank design and check that it saves and exports. Add a text box and a shape, then export the page. If the export works, the install is working. If it doesn't, check the copy in Applications first.
Then decide whether you need a paid plan. This guide doesn't list prices. Check Canva's pricing page before you choose, since the sources I found disagree on the Pro price.

If you design for clients or a team, [Canva for designers on Mac](/for/designers/canva) covers resizing, branding and exports. For a closer look at the assistant side, see [AI assistant for Canva on Mac](/apps/canva).

faq.question: Is the canva.com version the same as the Mac App Store version?
faq.answer: Both are the Canva desktop app for Mac. The App Store listing I checked shows version 1.127.0, released November 1. The canva.com page doesn't show a version, so I can't confirm the two files match. Pick one route and update it the way that route does.

faq.question: Which macOS version does Canva for Mac need?
faq.answer: The Mac App Store listing says macOS 13.0 or later. Some older guides list older versions, but the current listing is the one to trust. Check your version under Apple menu > About This Mac.

faq.question: Does Canva for Mac run on Apple silicon and Intel Macs?
faq.answer: Yes. Canva's download page says the app is available for Macs with Intel chips and Apple chips. The download link path says universal, so you don't pick a chip type.

faq.question: Why does my Mac say Apple cannot check Canva for malicious software?
faq.answer: That is Apple's generic alert for apps it can't check. It is not a Canva error message. Re-download from canva.com or the Mac App Store, then use Privacy & Security > Open Anyway only if the source is right.

faq.question: Why is Check for Updates missing from my Canva menu?
faq.answer: The item appears only when an update is available. If you installed from the App Store, look under the Updates tab in the App Store instead.

faq.question: Does the Canva desktop app need the internet?
faq.answer: The sources I checked agree that most features need a connection. They disagree on offline use, so test it yourself before you travel or rely on it.

faq.question: Can I install Canva with Homebrew?
faq.answer: A search result mentioned a Homebrew cask, but I did not verify it. Use canva.com or the Mac App Store, the two routes I checked.

faq.question: Is the iPhone Canva app the same as the Mac app?
faq.answer: No. The iPhone listing shares the app ID 897446215, but it shows version 4.234.0 for iPhone. The Mac listing shows version 1.127.0.

steps.name: Check your macOS version
steps.text: Click the Apple menu in the top left corner, then choose About This Mac. Read the macOS version. Canva's desktop app needs macOS 13.0 or later, according to the Mac App Store listing.
steps.tip: Apple silicon and Intel Macs both work. You don't need a separate download for each chip.

steps.name: Route A: open the Canva Mac download page
steps.text: Open Safari or another browser and go to canva.com/download/mac. Click Download Canva for Mac. The button links to a universal Mac file.
steps.tip: Type the address yourself if a link in an email or chat looks unfamiliar.

steps.name: Route A: wait for the file to finish downloading
steps.text: Watch the download in your browser. The App Store version of Canva is about 168 MB, so the web file may be a similar size. Keep the Mac awake until the download ends.

steps.name: Route A: open the downloaded file
steps.text: In Finder, choose Go > Downloads and find the Canva file. Double-click it. If it's a disk image ending in .dmg, wait for its window to open. Canva's page doesn't list the file type, so this step covers both cases.

steps.name: Route A: move Canva into Applications
steps.text: In the window that opens, drag the Canva icon onto the Applications folder. If the file is already an app, drag that app into Applications instead.
steps.tip: Launch Canva from Applications so you always open the installed copy.

steps.name: Open Canva from Applications
steps.text: In Finder, click Applications in the sidebar and double-click Canva. If macOS blocks the app with a warning, go to the next step.

steps.name: Allow Canva in Privacy & Security
steps.text: Close the warning. Click the Apple menu, then System Settings. Click Privacy & Security, scroll down to the message about Canva, and click Open Anyway.
steps.tip: Click Open Anyway only for a file you trust, such as the one from canva.com or the App Store.

steps.name: Confirm the second prompt
steps.text: macOS shows one more warning. Click Open. Canva launches, and Apple says the app is saved as an exception, so you should only need to do this once.
steps.tip: If the Open Anyway button doesn't appear, check the Allow apps downloaded from setting before you retry.

steps.name: Finish the first launch
steps.text: When Canva opens, follow the prompts it shows. Then open a blank design to confirm the app responds.

steps.name: Check for updates later
steps.text: For a canva.com install, click Canva in the menu bar and choose Check for Updates. The item appears only when an update exists.
steps.tip: This menu path comes from a third-party guide from October 2024. If your menu uses different names, follow what you see.

steps.name: Route B: install from the Mac App Store
steps.text: Open the App Store app and search for Canva. Choose the Mac listing from developer Canva. Click the button that offers the app, wait for the download, then open Canva from Applications.
steps.tip: Check that the listing is for Mac. The iPhone page uses the same app ID but shows a different version.

troubleshooting.problem: No Open Anyway button appears for Canva
troubleshooting.fix: Open System Settings > Privacy & Security and check Allow apps downloaded from. If an administrator set it, ask IT to approve Canva.

troubleshooting.problem: Apple cannot check Canva for malicious software
troubleshooting.fix: If you didn't download from canva.com or the App Store, move the file to the Trash and download again from one of them. If it came from those pages and the alert returns, ask IT before you retry.

troubleshooting.problem: The App Store shows a different version than my Mac
troubleshooting.fix: Check that you're on the Mac listing. The iPhone page shows version 4.234.0. The Mac listing I checked showed 1.127.0.

troubleshooting.problem: Check for Updates is missing from the Canva menu
troubleshooting.fix: That item appears only when an update exists. If you installed from the App Store, check the Updates tab instead.

troubleshooting.problem: My Mac runs a macOS version older than 13.0
troubleshooting.fix: Update macOS first if your Mac can take the update. The listing requires macOS 13.0 or later, so the desktop app won't run on an older release.
Canva's page doesn't say the file type. Try the Mac App Store route instead, or download the file again from canva.com/download/mac.
